h: Your Game Plan for The Cornerhouse
p: The Cornerhouse sits on Forman Street, just up from the Theatre Royal, and it's one of those buildings where you can quite happily lose an entire evening. That's the beauty of it: no traipsing between venues in the rain, no losing half your group on the way to the next bar. Everything's stacked up in one place, with the lanes doing the heavy lifting.

The easiest way in is by tram. The stop at the Royal Centre is right by the theatre, and the Old Market Square stop isn't much further, so you can get here from the station or from the park and ride sites without much fuss. If you're coming in from the suburbs for a night out, it saves arguing over who's driving.

Here's a running order that works well. Grab an early bite in the complex, bowl a couple of games while everyone's still fresh, then decide whether to stay for drinks or catch a late film. If you're out with a mixed group, bowling first is clever, as it breaks the ice for anyone who doesn't know each other yet. By the second game, everyone's mates.

A word on the area itself. This top end of the city centre is close to Nottingham Trent University's city campus, so it has a young, lively feel, especially during term time. Arboretum park, one of the oldest public parks in the city, is a short walk north and makes a pleasant green breather before heading back into the buzz. Shoes on, team names sorted, and away you go.
